beats.beat: In Winchester the next morning, the attorney confirms that the earlier will naming Farr was never formally revoked, only set aside as superseded.
He permits Judith and Farr to search a shelf of unclaimed correspondence kept at his office for want of a clear direction.
Among the letters they find Whitlow's own, misdirected there through a clerk's error rather than destroyed.
beats.note: The draft explains the misdirection as routine office procedure rather than an explicit clerk's mistake, a slight loosening of the beat's wording but the same narrative fact.

beats.beat: Its date proves that Fenner was already failing months before Hartwell's will was ever drawn up.
The attorney agrees to summon Hartwell to account, and Farr and Judith hurry back toward Amberlight before he can sell off the farm's stock.

turn.note: The auction bill for Thursday's sale forces immediate action, ending on Judith's order to ride back that night rather than wait on the attorney's letter.

trope_note: The disputed inheritance is the whole engine of the chapter and lands cleanly; the returning officer is present through Farr's stake but not foregrounded here; forced proximity is absent this chapter, which is appropriate since it belongs to the previous one.
length_note: Draft runs to roughly 768 words against a 560-word target, about 37% over, though the excess is mostly incident and evidentiary detail rather than padding.
fixes: Trim the Cobbold introduction paragraph (the fire, the clerk who writes standing, the buried-three-clients aside) by a third; it is atmosphere doing double duty as characterisation and can be cut to the single detail that earns its place.
Replace 'he was too old to be surprised by a farm' with something concrete to Cobbold specifically, not a stock lawyer trait.
Cut 'which Judith thought said a great deal about thirty years of practice' and let his stillness stand unglossed.
Tighten the dead-letter-office explanation paragraph; it can be delivered in two sentences instead of the current four.
Consider trimming the will-history paragraph in segment one, which restates the same fact (never revoked, only superseded) three times in slightly different words.
